conviction_note: Scaled number = (2*43/100-1)*10 = -1.4: abs_move 10 sits just above the 9.14 event-implied move (spread 54% of mid, indicative) and the 6.82 median reaction, because the FY guide is the swing and this name has moved 15-22% on guide shortfalls; p_up 43 leans down on the stretched H2 needed to hold the reiterated $850M-1B EBITDA guide, put skew +8.3 and 6 of 7 prior prints falling, and is held near 50 by an ~11-day-to-cover short on a small free float and an EPS bar I could not pin (8.34 vs 8.60). The findings sum (-0.2) is much smaller than the scaled number because the positioning and peer positives offset the guide-risk negative finding by finding, while the reaction history (which is not itself a finding) carries the lean in p_up.
bar: Company guide: FY2026 adjusted EBITDA $850M-$1.0B, reiterated on the Q2 call 2026-07-29 (https://transcripts.platformaeronaut.com/summaries/CAR-2Q26-AI-Summary; raised from $800M-1B on Q1, https://rallies.ai/news/avis-posts-70-first-quarter-utilization-record-raises-2026-ebitda-outlook), with Q3 guided to roughly flat RPD and an Americas fleet down mid-single digits. Q3 EPS consensus is disputed: Benzinga $8.34 non-GAAP vs another aggregator $8.5951 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CAR/earnings-forecasts, via search 2026-11-03); no Q3 revenue or EBITDA consensus found. The guide is sourced, the quarterly bar is not, so the reported-quarter findings are capped small. Arithmetic: H1 2026 adj EBITDA = -113 + 286 = $173M (Q1 and Q2 releases), so H2 must deliver $677-827M against H2 2025 of $564M (Q3 559 + Q4 5, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/723612/000072361226000010/a03-prxpressreleasexq4f25.htm).
positioning_check: FINRA settlement 2026-09-30: 5.25M shares short, 11.0 days to cover (https://massive.com/quote/car); Equibles model for 2026-10-15 ~5.41M (estimate, not reported: https://equibles.com/stocks/car/short-interest). Shares outstanding 35,325,754 at 2026-07-22 (Q2 10-Q cover), so ~15% of shares outstanding; the free float is much smaller because Pentwater (>19-22%) and other holders lock up a large block (April 2026 squeeze reports: 54% of free float short, https://rallies.ai/news/avis-budget-shares-surge-340-on-short-squeeze-atm-offering-to-raise-2b), so the short is crowded against the tradable float. Skew +8.3 vol points (25d put over call): downside is being paid. Put/call OI 0.68, total OI only 1,356 and ATM spread 54% of mid, so the option read is thin. Run-up +9.07% over 5 sessions (+6.3% on 2026-10-30 with no news found), -1.04% over 20, -84% off the 52w high from the squeeze.

findings.finding: Holding the reiterated FY2026 adj EBITDA guide of $850M-$1.0B requires H2 of $677-827M, +20% to +47% over H2 2025's $564M, while management guided Q3 RPD roughly flat and the Americas fleet down mid-single digits, and said forward bookings had eroded since early May; a guide cut toward or below $850M is the live risk on the line this stock trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026 print with a ~$150M Q4 shortfall vs guide and a $800M-1B first guide: -21.54%. Jul 2025 (-15.41%) and Jul 2026 (-6.9%, guide reiterated but demand softer) both fell. Q1 2026 guide raise to $850M-1B still fell 18% on a wider loss per chartmill, though the baseline's close-to-close shows -0.47%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the disputed EPS consensus ($8.34, below Q3 2025's level) suggests the Street already sits near or below the low end of the guide, and the put skew pays for downside. If a cut were fully priced, the stock would not have run +9% in five sessions into the print and consensus would sit openly below the guide-implied Q3; neither is visible.
findings.independence: H1 actuals from the company's own Q1 and Q2 releases (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000723612/000072361226000037/a03-pressreleasexq2f26.htm) and the Q4 2025 release for the H2 2025 base; the demand softening is echoed by an Auto Rental News headline of 2026-08-02, 'Avis Cuts Fleet as Summer Demand Trails Expectations' (headline only). The TSA and Manheim findings below are separate series feeding this same guide risk and are sized for their own quarter effect only.

findings.finding: TSA checkpoint volumes for 21 Jun-7 Sep 2026 were 204.15M against 209.91M in 2025 (-2.7%), August -4.4%; early September was flat (+0.2%). Airport rental days fall with them; Avis had already guided the fleet down mid-single digits for Q3, so most of this sits inside the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Rental-day/volume shortfalls fed the Feb 2026 (-21.54%) and Jul 2026 (-6.9%) declines; no isolated read for volume alone.
findings.source_date: 2026-09 (article covers through 2026-09-07; page returned 403, figures from search snippet, snippet_only)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: TSA data is public daily and the company pre-guided a smaller fleet. If the market saw volumes worse than guided, consensus would show visible downward revisions after September; I found none dated.
findings.independence: https://deeparrival.com/news/tsa-summer-checkpoint-traveler-volume-drop-2026/ (same TSA series, separate tally). Proxy, not company-confirmed; Hertz guided Q3 transaction days +~1%, which cuts the other way.

findings.finding: The Manheim used-vehicle index fell to 205.9 in September 2026, -0.6% y/y and -1.1% m/m, its first reading below year-ago in 2026, with SUV values pressured partly by younger rental-fleet supply; mid-October recovered to 207.4 (+2.2% y/y). That is a slight headwind to Q3 gains on sale and DPU, and neutral-to-positive for Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Higher depreciation and lower gains on sale were $60M of the ~$150M Q4 2025 shortfall, which drove the -21.54% reaction in Feb 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: A public series the sell side tracks, so mostly priced; the size of the September dip is small and the October rebound already offsets it.
findings.independence: Mid-October reading 207.4 (+2.2% y/y) from Cox Automotive's Oct 2026 mid-month report, https://www.coxautoinc.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/October-2026-Mid-Month-Market-Insights.pdf (via search snippet; PDF unreadable).

findings.finding: Hertz, the direct peer, spoke after Avis (2026-08-06): Q2 RPD +9% and RPU +8% on 'a more balanced industry supply-demand environment', a small World Cup benefit, 'forward views on residual values remain stable', and Q3 adj corporate EBITDA guided at $275-325M with transaction days up ~1%. That is a more constructive industry pricing read than Avis's own flat-RPD Q3 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history of CAR reacting to an RPD surprise in the baseline; Q1 2026's +3% RPD beat came with an -0.47% close-to-close reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Three months old and public. The part that may not be priced is that Avis guided RPD flat on 2026-07-29 before Hertz described a firmer industry; if the market had taken that read, CAR would not trade at a flat-RPD-implied consensus below last year. Hertz's own Q3 print is 2026-11-05, after this window.
findings.independence: Hertz Q3 guidance $275-325M and transaction days ~+1% also via https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2972207/hertz-global-stock-rises-124-since-q2-earnings-release. Partly Hertz-specific (its own fleet-rotation turnaround), so the transmission to Avis pricing is a proxy.

findings.finding: Short interest is 5.25M shares (2026-09-30 settlement) with 11.0 days to cover on ~394k average daily volume, against a free float much smaller than the 35.3M shares outstanding; any print that holds the guide forces cover into thin turnover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The same crowded short did not prevent -6.9% (Jul 2026) or -21.54% (Feb 2026) on weak guides; it fed the April 2026 squeeze outside earnings. So the squeeze needs a non-negative print to act.
findings.why_not_priced: The +9% five-day run-up into the print may be early covering, so partly priced. If the squeeze risk were fully priced, call skew would be bid relative to puts; instead the 25d skew is +8.3 toward puts.
findings.independence: Equibles model for the 2026-10-15 settlement ~5.41M (rising): https://equibles.com/stocks/car/short-interest. Aug 14 settlement 5.4M at 15.8 DTC: https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/car/short-interest/.

findings.finding: Avis received the $650M Pentwater Section 16(b) settlement in cash on 2026-10-05 (about $18 a share, ~16% of the ~$3.9B market cap), to be recognized in Q4, and on 2026-11-02 gave notice to redeem the remaining $350M of 5.75% notes due 2027 at par on 2026-12-30. Net corporate leverage was 7.4x against a target of at least one turn lower by year-end, so the call may give a pro forma leverage number or a use for the ~$300M remainder.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The settlement announcement produced a +5.22% overnight rise (https://www.itiger.com/news/1104931090); the baseline carries no print reaction on a balance-sheet item.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: both 8-Ks are public. What is not public is any use of the remaining ~$300M (deleveraging vs buyback); a buyback on a tiny float with 11 days of short would be visible as upside, but nothing says one is coming. Below operating income and outside adjusted EBITDA, so sized as a fraction.
findings.independence: Redemption notice 8-K 2026-11-02: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/723612/000095014226002911/eh260848006_8k.htm (same programme, same company; one fact chain).

findings.finding: On 2026-09-21 Avis closed a $650M five-year AESOP Series 2026-5 fleet ABS (Class A $474.5M at 5.69%, Class D at 8.14%): routine fleet financing with market access intact, no stated distress use.
findings.why_not_priced: Public 8-K, a routine fleet-funding renewal. What the money buys: vehicles for the domestic fleet, consistent with a fleet held down mid-single digits rather than a ramp. Signed zero after asking.
findings.independence: Q2 10-Q: $1,867M vehicle-program capacity available, covenants in compliance (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000723612/000072361226000039/car-20260630.htm).

findings.finding: EVP and Chief Digital & Innovation Officer Ravi Simhambhatla left on 2026-09-30, with no successor named (8-K item 5.02, 2026-09-01).
findings.why_not_priced: Public for two months and a non-financial officer; included only so a judge can see it. Nearly zero.

outside_window.finding: Hertz reports Q3 2026 at 08:00 ET on 2026-11-05, after the CAR exit window closes on 2026-11-04; its industry RPD and DPU read cannot inform this trade.
Redemption of the $350M 5.75% 2027 notes settles 2026-12-30; the settlement cash is recognized in Q4 financials (the cash and the notice are already public and filed above as a one-off).

baseline_tension: The guide-risk finding and the 6-of-7-down reaction history agree with the +8.3 put skew; the five-day +9% run-up and the crowded, low-float short cut against them. So the downside lean is mostly in the price, and p_up sits only 7 points below 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar unsourced: EPS $8.34 vs $8.60, no revenue or EBITDA consensus): reported-quarter findings capped smaller (TSA -0.7 to -0.4, Manheim -0.3 to -0.2), and p_up moved from 42 to 43.
Rule 7 (crowded short against a negative): the guide-risk finding was cut from -1.5 to -1.2. It kept its sign because the skew agrees with it.
Rule 5 (a peer is a proxy for this company): the Hertz finding was cut from +0.8 to +0.6, since Hertz's RPD gain is partly its own turnaround.
Rule 2 (one-off below operating income): the settlement and redemption were cut from +0.5 to +0.3, with the deleveraging path stated.
Rule 5 / core (positioning files): the short-interest finding was cut from +1.0 to +0.8, since the run-up may already be early covering.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the ABS stayed at 0 after asking what it buys (routine fleet funding for a smaller fleet).
